WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Ezekiel son of Buzi; Four living creatures

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.
- Four living creatures: adult beings of ageless bearing; each has the likeness of a man in form, with four faces of man, lion, ox and eagle, and four wings. Skin is bronze-gold, burnished like coals; hair fine and flowing; eyes bright as torchlight. One signature outfit: no garment, only the wings and the bright radiance of fire about them, colours of gold, bronze and smoky flame. Signature prop: none, but each bears a wheel like beryl stone beside it.
- River Chebar: a slow, broad canal-river of the Babylonian plain, its brown-green water running between low earthen banks lined with reeds, date palms and willows. Mud-brick and fired-brick settlements of the exile stand on rising ground above the flood line, with irrigation channels, earthen dykes and walled fields stretching flat to the horizon.
- Only Ezekiel son of Buzi, Four living creatures, River Chebar have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Ezekiel kneeling or standing on the riverbank, looking up in awe
Action: Radiant light and fire gather in a shining, throne-like form above the sapphire-blue expanse, with no visible figure within it
Setting: Reed-lined bank of the Chebar canal beside a mud-brick settlement in Babylonian exile
Secondary elements: Four winged living creatures beneath the expanse, their wings lowered; amber fire and cloud rising from the north; river reeds bent by wind
Mood: Awe, reverence and tense wonder
Time of day: Dawn brightening into daylight, clear air with a rising storm wind
Composition: Low viewpoint from the riverbank looking upward, Ezekiel small in the lower frame, the expanse and radiant throne-light filling the upper frame

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. Describe only the shared place, weather and light. Where the section shows one of them, its presence may appear only as smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light spread through the place. Never describe its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train, face, hands, hair, body or silhouette, even as an empty seat, a denial or a figure made of light: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.
